title.en: Justice for the Poor and the Wronged

heading.en: Acquitting the guilty, condemning the innocent

body.en:
'Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent — the Lord detests them both.' Proverbs treats injustice in BOTH directions as equally wrong — letting the guilty go free is just as bad as punishing someone innocent.

'To do what is right and just is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.' Even religious devotion, Proverbs suggests, matters less to God than simple, practical justice and fairness toward others.

'To show partiality in judging is not good... whoever says to the guilty, "You are innocent" will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations.' Favouritism in judgment is treated as a serious moral failure, not a small bias.

'The righteous care about justice for the poor, but the wicked have no such concern.' Genuine righteousness, in Proverbs' view, is measured partly by whether someone actually cares about fairness for people with less power.

'Whoever says to the wicked, "You are innocent," will be cursed by peoples, denounced by nations, but those who convict the guilty will fare well and have a rich blessing come on them.' Standing firmly for what's actually true and fair, even when it's unpopular, leads to genuine blessing.

verse.en: The righteous care about justice for the poor, but the wicked have no such concern.

title.en: A Song for Justice for the Poor and the Wronged

q.en: What does Proverbs 17:15 say the Lord detests, regarding the guilty and the innocent?

en: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent — both detested equally

q.en: According to Proverbs 21:3, what does the Lord value even more than sacrifice?

en: Doing what is right and just

en: The righteous care about justice for the poor; the wicked have no such concern
The wicked care more about justice
Justice doesn't matter to either group

label.en: Activity sheet: Justice for the Poor and the Wronged

body.en:
Big idea: genuine righteousness, in Proverbs' view, is inseparable from a concern for justice and fairness, especially toward those with less power — and this concern is valued by God even above religious ritual or sacrifice. Injustice in either direction (excusing the guilty or condemning the innocent) is treated with equal seriousness, refusing any convenient bias.

Conversation starters: (1) Why might Proverbs say doing what's right and just matters even more to God than religious sacrifice? (2) What does it mean that excusing the guilty is just as wrong as condemning the innocent? (3) What's one situation where you could actively "care about justice" for someone with less power or voice?

Pray for hearts that genuinely care about fairness and justice, especially for those who are often overlooked.
